topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic changes and cellular conditions underlying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable the evolution of cancer in susceptible cells within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposure contributes to variation in cancer risk rather than cancer being attributable solely to chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of infection-dependent carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become mutations, often through the body's own metabolic processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-driven initiation from the promotion of tumour growth and explain why a permissive environment can be necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Biological context and susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and consolidate how the biological conditions of exposure determine whether carcinogenic damage leads to cancer.

topics.label: Evidence linking human carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine experimental tests of carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of judging those risks against benefits.
